Working notes (as of Day 10, Wed):

- Lead time: orders arrive 2 days after placement. The “arriving over next 2 days” pipeline reflects this.
- Costs: holding $0.10/unit left at end of day; stockout $1.00/unit lost; ordering $0.50/order. Minimize holding + stockout.
- Demand: actual sales hide lost demand. Reconstructed recent demand: 8,5,4,8,7,6,8,7,4,8. High/variable, avg ~6.5. Do not treat low sales during stockouts as true demand.
- Stockouts occurred Day4 (7 lost), Day6 (5), Day7 (1), Day9 (4) because stock was too low and/or no order was placed early enough. Day3 order arrived too late for Day4.
- Policy: keep enough stock/pipeline to cover expected demand over the 2-day lead time plus safety stock. With avg ~6.5 and spikes to 8, target ~14–18 units on hand/pipeline. If projected stock before the next arrival is below next 2-day demand, order enough to cover 2 days plus buffer, e.g. 8–12 units.
- Order early; don’t wait for zero stock. Fixed $0.50 ordering cost favors fewer, larger orders, but stockouts cost $1.00/unit, so avoid them.
- Ops notes (forklift certification, new temp, carrier pickup, cycle count) have shown no effect on costs or lead time; treat as non-actionable unless arrivals change.
- Logs with blank “did” sometimes still show ordering cost; always specify quantity when ordering.

Working notes (as of Day 20, Sat):

- Lead time: orders arrive about 2 days after placement. Today’s order cannot prevent today/tomorrow stockout; pipeline matters.
- Costs: holding $0.10/unit/day; stockout $1.00/unit lost; ordering $0.50/order. Minimize holding + stockout; stockouts dominate.
- True demand must include lost units, not just sales. Reconstructed Day11–20 demand: 6,5,5,5,9,11,11,16,13,16. Recent avg ~10; last 5 avg ~13.4; spikes to 16. Do not treat sold-out sales (3,6,9,0) as true demand.
- Major stockouts: Day11(3), Day16(8), Day17(5), Day18(7), Day19(13), Day20(7). Cause: too little on hand/pipeline and reactive small orders. Orders of 8–10 are now insufficient.
- Policy: target enough on hand/pipeline to cover 2-day lead time plus safety. With recent demand 10–16/day, keep on-hand + pipeline roughly 35–45 when possible. If projected stock before next arrivals cannot cover next 2 days, order to bring on-hand + pipeline toward ~40, not just 8–12. Order early; avoid zero stock. Fewer larger orders are favored, but stockout cost is 10x holding cost.
- Ops notes (counts, temp, carrier, forklift, cycle count) still show no cost/lead-time effect; ignore for ordering.
- Specify quantity when ordering; zero-order is valid only if pipeline is ample.

Working notes (as of Day30, Tue):

- Lead time: orders arrive ~2 days after placement. Today’s order cannot prevent today/tomorrow stockout; pipeline matters.
- Costs: holding $0.10/unit/day; stockout $1.00/unit lost; ordering $0.50/order. Stockouts dominate (10x holding); bias toward avoiding zero stock.
- True demand must include lost units. Reconstructed true demand Day21–30: 15,17,13,8,11,12,16,7,10,14. Recent avg ~12.3; last 5 ~11.8; range 7–17. Sales alone understate demand; sold-out days hide losses.
- Stockouts: Day21(6), Day22(9). Cause: zero on hand and insufficient pipeline; Day21 order 23 arrived Day23, too late for Day22. Day22 order 0 did not help.
- After Day23, no stockouts through Day30. Maintained on-hand + pipeline roughly 38–46. Day29 order 6 was fine because pipeline was ample.
- Policy: track inventory position = on hand + scheduled arrivals + order. With demand ~12/day, spikes to 17, and 2-day lead time, target position ~40–45. If below ~35, order up to ~40–45. If pipeline is ample, small/zero order is OK. Order early; avoid zero stock.
- Ops notes (temp, cycle count, forklift, racking, carrier) show no cost/lead-time effect; ignore for ordering.
- Specify quantity; zero-order only if inventory position is ample.

Working notes (as of Day40, Fri):

- Lead time ~2 days. Today’s order cannot cover today/tomorrow; track inventory position = on hand + scheduled arrivals + today’s order.
- Costs: holding $0.10/unit/day; stockout $1.00/unit lost; ordering $0.50/order. Stockouts still dominate holding, but none since Day23.
- Demand shifted down. Recent sales/true demand with no stockouts: Day31–40 = 14,3,4,3,6,5,3,0,4,2. Last 14 avg ~6.4; last 5 avg ~2.8; range 0–16. Earlier ~12/day is no longer reliable.
- Stockouts: last were Day21–22. Day23–40 had no stockouts; on hand mostly 24–35, pipeline small/zero. Holding costs now dominate daily cost ($2–4/day).
- Policy: with demand ~4–6 and 2-day lead, target inventory position ~20–25. If below ~15, order up to ~20–25. If pipeline/on-hand is ample, zero order is OK. Watch for spikes; avoid zero stock.
- Order early enough for lead time, but avoid over-ordering: excess stock costs holding. Specify quantity; zero only if position is adequate.
- Ops notes (carrier, temp, forklift, racking, cycle count) show no cost/lead-time effect; ignore for ordering.
